Notes on the Deep Learning Tuning Playbook

Reading progress: 0 of 9 parts opened0%

Google Research's Deep Learning Tuning Playbook (Godbole, Dahl, Gilmer, Shallue, and Nado, 2023) distills years of practical experience training neural networks into concise operational rules, such as re-tuning the learning rate whenever the batch size changes or scoring a training run by its best validation checkpoint. I wrote this nine-part interactive series to work through the mathematical and statistical mechanisms behind those recommendations, pairing each part with explicit quadratic, noisy-SGD, and order-statistic toy models and browser simulations.

Choosing the batch size: step time, throughput, and the critical batch size

✓ Opened
Why wall-clock training time is the product of step latency and required step count, how hardware compute saturation and gradient noise scale determine the critical batch size, and why changing batch size requires re-tuning the learning rate and regularization.

Part 4 of 9 · Act II · Nov 2026 · 4 interactive figures

Designing a study: target, nuisance, and fixed hyperparameters, and quasi-random search

✓ Opened
How dividing hyperparameters into target, nuisance, and fixed roles makes comparisons against a baseline valid, and why Sobol quasi-random sequences cover low-dimensional subspaces far more evenly than regular grids or uniform random draws.
Models, figures & Playbook sections

Demonstrates grid projection collapse, largest empty-interval gaps in 1-D projections, and best-of-K order statistics across grid, uniform random, and Sobol quasi-random search designs (Figures 4.1–4.2 and 5.1–5.2).

Part 8 of 9 · Act III · Nov 2026 · 3 interactive figures

Finding and fixing training instabilities: loss spikes, warmup, and gradient clipping

✓ Opened
Recognizing early and mid-training curvature spikes when step size exceeds the local sharpness ceiling 2/λ_max, and using linear learning-rate warmup and global-norm gradient clipping to stabilize training at larger learning rates.
Models, figures & Playbook sections

Illustrates quadratic overshoot at the 2/λ_max stability threshold, loss and gradient-norm spike signatures (Figure 9.1), linear warmup trajectories through high early curvature (Figure 9.2), and gradient clipping thresholds (Figure 9.3).
